manual_only.claim: 6060 modes 1 position, 3 velocity, 6 homing; 6061 is observed mode. The translated set instruction for 6061 is unresolved
Controlword 6, 7, 15 is a state-transition example with approximately 10 ms between writes, not a universal startup script
Position target and profile velocity/ramp tables state native limits and milliseconds; pulse graph does not prove feedback scale
Controlword bit 4 rising edge is described as a new-target trigger
Controlword bit 5 distinguishes after-current-curve and immediate update
Controlword bit 6 distinguishes absolute and relative examples
Examples 15 to 31/95/63/127 combine trigger, coordinate and update bits; current state remains a prerequisite
15 to 271 is called stop in Chinese/operating tables; missing from EN86 transition table; 605D options and stop effect remain unresolved
15 to 11 is called emergency stop; no stop latency or safety rating is established
Statusword bit definitions differ among the 86C manuals; preserve raw status and each source interpretation
Procedure table calls target velocity U32 0..3000 rpm while dictionary/EDS call it I32; ramps are milliseconds
EN86 enables before target parameters; ZH86 and OP86 specify parameters before 6 to 7 to 15
Methods 17/18/24/29, two U32 speeds and U32 ramp time, plus home offset are described; physical prerequisites remain method-specific
Method 17 searches negative limit, withdraws positive and creeps negative toward limit
Method 18 searches positive limit, withdraws negative and creeps positive toward limit
Method 24 searches positive origin, withdraws negative and creeps positive toward origin
Method 29 searches negative origin and creeps positive until leaving switch
Controlword bit 4 transition 0 to 1 starts homing; 1 to 0 is described as stop/interruption, with resulting reference unresolved
Manuals call statusword bit 8 homing completion; speed/running bit claims differ
2302 0 to 1 clears current position, followed by manual return to zero; coordinate/reference effects need review
2300 value 2 is described as saving parameters through SDO; completion time is not documented
2300 value 1 is called restore factory parameters, zero ineffective; resulting settings/state need review
Controlword bit 7 and 15 to 128 example are separate fault-reset claims; return-to-zero edge is described
2301 value 1 is described as effective fault reset, zero ineffective; equivalence to controlword reset is unproven
2100 bits 0..6 describe in-position, homed, running, alarm, released and two software limits; EDS says RW
2101 bits 0..6 describe logical input active states; physical voltage interpretation is separate
2102 bits 0..2 describe logical output active states, distinct from 60FE bits 16..18
2200 labels Pulse Sign and Pulse /Sign; positive shaft direction remains unresolved
2201 has conflicting documented ranges; command, feedback and encoder-count scaling remain unresolved
2202 options 0/1 and 607D limits are documented; EDS default 10 conflicts
2203 range includes 0; DIP precedence, activation and reset/save behavior are not established
2400:01 bits 0..6 invert logical DI states according to manual; physical wiring remains separate
2400:02..08 describe origin, positive/negative limit, enable, stop, emergency stop and user inputs
Manuals call 2400:0A an input filter coefficient and list 2401..2407 per-input filters; no time unit/equation established
Manuals disagree with EDS on 2400:0B versus 0C; tables describe only bits 0/1 despite three outputs
2400:0C..0F meanings and function numbers 2/3 conflict across source tables
OP86 describes 60FE:01 physical outputs and :02 mask at bits 16..18; both corresponding bits must be 1 to command an output. Terminal identity remains unqualified.
DO2/function 5 relay example says PA_01E while same-page table says PA_02E; not a new CANopen object
2500 0 ineffective, 1 open loop, 2 closed loop is distinct from 6060 motion mode
2501 names encoder resolution without line/count/quadrature basis
2502 is mA, 2503..2506 percent ratios and 2507 milliseconds; motor ratings remain independent
2508..2519 describe filters, thresholds and gains; EDS-only 251A..2520 have no reviewed physical meaning
603F table names FF01 overcurrent and FF05 excessive position deviation within FF00..FFFF
Per-five-second LED counts 1..5 distinguish power-restart faults from resettable faults
SW1..5 encode 1..31; all OFF selects user-defined node, not node zero
SW6/SW7 choose 125/250/500/1000 kbit/s; EDS advertises 50 kbit/s without manual DIP choice
SW8 ON connects 120 ohms; RJ45 pins 1/2/3 are CAN_H/CAN_L/GND; cable lengths are recommendations
Manuals describe seven 24 V inputs, DICOM wiring, DOCOM 0 V and three outputs; actual fixture unknown
Cover/product table names CiA301/CiA402.V2, three motion modes, 32-axis claim and dual RJ45; no universal CAN assumptions follow
Supply ranges conflict between product table and wiring/terminal pages; no bench default follows
ZH57 statusword table assigns bit 7 to alarm/ready; this 57C model contrast does not establish a CL86-C status mask
ZH57 p8 identifies 60FE bits 16..18 as DO0..DO2, while p17 calls them DO1..DO3; preserve physical identity conflict
ZH57 product and terminal pages give different DC supply ranges; neither sets a bench default
